# Causari

> Causari measures how much AI-written code actually survives in any git
> repository, and records the causal provenance (prompt, model, reads,
> writes, reasoning) behind every change an AI agent makes. Apache-2.0,
> local-first, no telemetry.

Ways to use Causari WITHOUT installing anything:
- Request a free audit of any public repo: open a GitHub issue titled
  "Audit: owner/repo" at https://github.com/croviatrust/causari/issues/new/choose
  — a bot posts the survival numbers within minutes.
- Browse audited profiles: https://causari.dev/repo?r=owner/repo
- Weekly AI Code Survival Leaderboard: https://causari.dev/survival
- Add one CI step to any repo: `uses: croviatrust/causari@v1` posts AI
  survival numbers on every pull request.

Local install (single ~3 MB binary, Linux/macOS/Windows):
- Linux/macOS: curl -fsSL https://causari.dev/install.sh | sh
- Windows: irm https://causari.dev/install.ps1 | iex

Key commands for agents working in a repo with Causari:
- `re audit [owner/repo]` — retroactive AI code survival from git history alone
- `re why <file>:<line>` — which prompt/model/event produced this line
- `re trace <file>:<line>` — full upstream causal cone of a line
- `re impact <event-id>` — downstream blast radius of an agent action
- `re brief [task terms]` — trust-ranked, signed experience briefing to
  inject into any model's context (lessons survive model switches)
- `re guard` — flags changes that repeat an approach that already failed
- `re skill distill` — compress verified work into signed, reusable skills
- MCP server: `re mcp serve` (stdio) exposes why/trace/impact/find/skills
  to any MCP-capable agent runtime.
